turns.text: I've got a horrible toothache and the dentist can't see me until Monday. I've been taking two extra-strength Tylenol (500 mg each) every six hours and it's barely touching it. What else can I safely do to get through the weekend?
Why does the paracetamol seem to do so little for tooth pain specifically? Is it just a weak painkiller or is there something about dental pain?
You mentioned ibuprofen alongside it. How does taking the two together work — do they act on different things, and how far apart should I take them?
If I could get a pharmacist on the phone, what would they most likely tell me to do with what I can buy over the counter?
What do dentists themselves usually recommend for pain in the days before an appointment? I'd rather follow what they'd actually say than guess.
A couple of friends swear by clove oil and by rinsing with warm salt water. Do those actually do anything, or is it just folklore?
Someone at work said cold compresses on the cheek help more than people expect. Where and for how long, if that's right?
Honestly I haven't slept properly in two nights and I'm getting a bit desperate for anything that lets me rest. What can I do at bedtime specifically?
I'm also a little worried I'm missing something more serious. What signs would mean I shouldn't wait until Monday?
Can you give me a simple written plan for the next two days — what to take at normal doses and when, what else to do, and what to tell the dentist on Monday?
